name: the-chief
description: The Chief: run agent squads from inside Claude Code. Per-task lanes (CLI, model, effort, agent count), a live view of every agent and subagent with stop and follow-up, Sonnet overviews kept by date with a day-end summary, and goals you start as /goal.

language.title: Language
language.description: auto (default): Turkish when Claude Code's language setting or the system is Turkish, else English. en or tr fixes it.

simple_mode.title: Simple mode
simple_mode.description: On: the fine-tuning options below are read as their defaults, whatever is saved (compact and read guards, handoff, wake guard, heavy command gate, stale locks, agents across all chats, allowed worker models, subagent routes, release of finished chiefs). Keys, models, tiers, permissions and money options are never touched. Off: every option is used as saved.

chief_work.title: How chiefs work
chief_work.description: either (default): each chief decides per piece whether to do it itself or hand it to workers. self: chiefs do the job themselves and start no workers. delegate: chiefs only split the job and hand it to workers. The leader can still say otherwise for one chief.

auto_pin.title: Pin chats automatically
auto_pin.description: off (default): The Chief never pins or unpins a chat by itself. on: a chat that does real work is pinned, and unpinned again when it sits idle.

auto_title.title: Name chats automatically
auto_title.description: off (default): The Chief never renames a chat by itself; a title you or the leader give stays. on: a chat is named once after its first request or goal.

show_row.title: Row above the chat
show_row.description: on (default): The Chief's one row above the chat box (The Chief button and running agents). off: the row is hidden for good; everything else keeps working. /chief-row off and /chief-row on change it too.

chief_remote_control.title: Remote Control
chief_remote_control.description: off (default): The Chief never turns Remote Control on by itself. on: every working chat turns its Remote Control on, so you can follow it from your phone.

health_check.title: CLI health check
health_check.description: auto: once a day each installed, signed-in agent CLI says one word on a small model, so a broken sign-in, key or empty credit shows before a job lands on it (it is taken out of the routes and you are told the fix). logins: only the free sign-in status, no test run. off: nothing runs by itself. /chief-check and the Settings button always test now.

max_parallel.title: Agents at once
max_parallel.description: At most this many headless agents run together; more wait in the queue. Launches also wait while less than the RAM reserve (ram_reserve_gb) would be left.

ram_reserve_gb.title: RAM kept free (GB)
ram_reserve_gb.description: New agents wait in the queue while launching them would leave less than this much available RAM. Agents grow after they start, so the machine stays responsive. Default 3.

anthropic_api_key.title: Claude Code API key
anthropic_api_key.description: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY for Claude Code agents. Empty uses your Claude login.

openai_api_key.title: Codex API key
openai_api_key.description: OPENAI_API_KEY for Codex agents. Empty uses your Codex login.

devin_api_key.title: Devin API key
devin_api_key.description: Passed to Devin agents as DEVIN_API_KEY.

qoder_api_key.title: Qoder token
qoder_api_key.description: Passed to Qoder agents as QODER_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN.

gemini_api_key.title: Gemini API key
gemini_api_key.description: Passed to Gemini CLI agents as GEMINI_API_KEY. Empty uses your Google login.

opencode_zen_api_key.title: OpenCode Zen API key
opencode_zen_api_key.description: Passed to OpenCode Zen agents as OPENCODE_API_KEY.

opencode_go_api_key.title: OpenCode Go API key
opencode_go_api_key.description: Passed to OpenCode Go agents as OPENCODE_API_KEY.

custom_api_key.title: Custom endpoint API key
custom_api_key.description: CUSTOM_API_KEY for the custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

anthropic_endpoint.title: Claude Code endpoint
anthropic_endpoint.description: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL for Claude Code agents. Empty is the default.

openai_endpoint.title: Codex endpoint
openai_endpoint.description: OPENAI_BASE_URL for Codex agents. Empty is the default.

custom_endpoint.title: Custom endpoint
custom_endpoint.description: An OpenAI-compatible base URL, e.g. https://host/v1.

claude_models.title: Claude Code models
claude_models.description: Models offered for Claude Code lanes, comma separated. Empty uses the built-in list.

codex_models.title: Codex models
codex_models.description: Models offered for Codex lanes, comma separated. Empty uses the built-in list.

devin_models.title: Devin models
devin_models.description: Models offered for Devin lanes, comma separated. Empty uses the built-in list.

cursor_models.title: Cursor models
cursor_models.description: Models offered for Cursor lanes, comma separated. Empty uses the built-in list.

qoder_models.title: Qoder models
qoder_models.description: Models offered for Qoder lanes, comma separated. Empty uses the built-in list.

gemini_models.title: Gemini models
gemini_models.description: Models offered for Gemini lanes, comma separated. Empty uses the built-in list.

antigravity_models.title: Antigravity models
antigravity_models.description: Models offered for Antigravity (agy) lanes, comma separated. Empty uses the built-in list; agy models prints them.

openrouter_models.title: OpenRouter models
openrouter_models.description: Models offered for OpenRouter lanes, comma separated. Empty uses the built-in list.

opencode_zen_models.title: OpenCode Zen models
opencode_zen_models.description: Models offered for OpenCode Zen lanes, comma separated. Empty uses the built-in list.

opencode_go_models.title: OpenCode Go models
opencode_go_models.description: Models offered for OpenCode Go lanes, comma separated. Empty uses the built-in list.

custom_models.title: Custom models
custom_models.description: Models offered for Custom lanes, comma separated. Empty uses the built-in list.

live_url.title: Live page
live_url.description: A claude.ai artifact link The Chief mirrors to, for your phone. Set it with /chief live <link>.

live_page.title: Live page
live_page.description: auto makes your private live page once (from the template the plugin ships, no model tokens) and pins it in your claude.ai sidebar; off never makes one.

summary_engine.title: Agent status lines
summary_engine.description: ask (default): never download; use a local model only if one is already here, else rules. auto: a small local model sums up each agent; The Chief finds one already running or downloads and sets up its own once (about 0.5-1.3 GB, GPU when there is one). rules: never a model. haiku: Claude Haiku. (The session title is always written by Haiku at low effort.)

local_model.title: Local model
local_model.description: qwen3.5-2b (1.3 GB, better summaries) or qwen3.5-0.8b (0.5 GB, lighter).

local_device.title: Local model device
local_device.description: auto: a discrete GPU (NVIDIA, AMD, Arc) when one has 2.5 GB free, else the CPU. cpu: always the CPU.

dev_source.title: Hot-reload source
dev_source.description: A folder with a newer The Chief build; /hot-reload copies it in and reloads.

reload_nonce.title: Reload marker
reload_nonce.description: Set by /hot-reload; changing it reloads The Chief in every session.

context_guard.title: Compact at
context_guard.description: After a turn, compact the chat once its context passes this many tokens (e.g. 300k). Every turn re-reads the whole context, so smaller is cheaper. off: only Claude Code's own auto-compact near the window.

cold_guard.title: Compact a cold chat at
cold_guard.description: When a chat sits idle past its 1-hour prompt cache (and less than 8 hours), compact it once while idle if its context is at least this big (e.g. 80k; default 80k), so the next message writes a summary instead of the whole history again. off: never.

read_guard.title: Cap whole-file reads at
read_guard.description: A Read of a text file bigger than this (e.g. 64k bytes) with no offset or limit reads only its head and says how to get the rest. off: never cap.

handoff_after_compacts.title: Hand off after compacts
handoff_after_compacts.description: After this many normal compacts (the size guard; cold and manual ones do not count) a session writes a detailed handoff file and a fresh session takes over, instead of compacting again. Default off. 0 or off: never.

handoff_after_hours.title: Hand off after hours
handoff_after_hours.description: A session alive longer than this many hours whose context is over 200k hands off the same way at the end of a turn. Default off. 0 or off: never.

wake_guard.title: No short wake loops
wake_guard.description: on (default): ScheduleWakeup with a delay under 5 minutes and scheduled tasks (CronCreate) that repeat more often than every 5 minutes are refused, since each wake-up re-reads the whole chat. off: allowed.

stale_locks.title: Stale lock paths
stale_locks.description: Lock files or folders your own scripts and worker briefs use (separated by ;), e.g. C:/repo/locks/tsc;C:/repo/locks/heavy.lock. Every 2 minutes one older than 15 minutes is removed when no heavy command (tsc, vitest, depcruise, test, bench) runs on this computer, or at once when the process id written in it is gone. The Chief's own heavy lock is freed the same way when the chat holding it is gone.

heavy_gate.title: Heavy command gate
heavy_gate.description: on (default): heavy commands (tsc, vitest, dependency-cruiser, ffmpeg) are held machine-wide, whoever started them, when the free RAM has no slot for them: the newest is paused and goes on, oldest first, when one ends (slots = (free RAM + RAM they hold − reserve) / 3.5 GB, 1-4). A command paused 30 minutes goes on anyway. Under 1.8 GB free one heavy tree a step is ended (the newest vitest first; never ffmpeg, never the last build). off: no gate.

subagent_tiers.title: Subagent tiers
subagent_tiers.description: JSON written by /chief Settings: for cok_zor (very hard), zor (hard), orta (medium) and kolay (easy) a CLI, model and effort. Once saved, spawn_worker takes a tier, Claude Code's Agent tool is held to these tiers, and every session is told. Empty: no tiers.

chief_tiers.title: Chief tiers
chief_tiers.description: JSON written by /chief Settings: the Claude model and effort of a chief chat per tier. Empty uses the defaults (opus-5-5 medium, sonnet-5-5 medium, sonnet-5-5 medium, haiku-5-5 max).

difficulty_floors.title: Difficulty floors
difficulty_floors.description: JSON written by /chief Settings: keywords that lift a job to at least a tier. Empty uses the defaults (video, edit, kurgu, reel, montaj, caption, thumbnail → zor (hard); upwork, başvuru, proposal → orta (medium)).

max_parallel_total.title: Agents at once, all chats
max_parallel_total.description: At most this many headless agents across every chat on this computer; empty means no shared ceiling.

claude_permission.title: Claude workers may
claude_permission.description: acceptEdits (default): create and edit files in their folder; shell commands that need approval are refused. bypassPermissions: everything, no questions (your choice). auto: asks, which a headless worker cannot answer.

chief_permission_mode.title: New chiefs start in
chief_permission_mode.description: off (default): a new chief chat opens in the app's default mode and asks before acting. auto: it opens in auto mode, with no approval cards. Asked once in the first-run setup.

worker_models.title: Allowed worker models
worker_models.description: Off (off, default): every model runs. If you write a list (cli/model, comma separated, cheapest to strongest), only the jobs the plugin picks itself (started with a tier, with no CLI or model name) are limited to this list, and on an error they move down this list. A CLI and model that the chief or you ask for by name always runs as asked and is never switched to another model. A private (private/confidential/client) job never drops to a free model, even if one is on the list.

consultants.title: Consultants
consultants.description: Models asked for a second opinion, in order (cli/model or cli/model:effort, comma separated). The chief asks the first one when you ask, before a decision that is hard to undo, on an error not solved in two tries, or for heavy analysis; if no answer comes, it moves to the next. A consultant runs read-only and changes no files. off = off. From the chat: /consult <question>.

worker_routes.title: Subagent routes
worker_routes.description: auto (default): when spawn_worker gets a tier it picks the CLI itself (easy = Qoder Qwen3.8-Flash / Longcat 2.5, medium = Longcat 2.5 / DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, hard = DeepSeek V4.1 Flash / Sonnet 5.5, very hard = Qoder Qwen3.8-Max / Sonnet 5.5; a CLI whose limit is used up is skipped; for private data a free route that keeps data is skipped). off: the saved Subagent tiers.

auto_release_done.title: Release finished chiefs
auto_release_done.description: auto (default): a chief that says DONE, is idle and has no agents is released by itself after 90 s (unpin + archive); it costs the leader no extra turn. off: the leader calls release_chief by hand.

tab_bridge.title: Chrome tab bridge
tab_bridge.description: off (default): agents never use your Chrome. on: The Chief installs its bundled bridge (in ~/.the-chief/tab-bridge, or LOCALAPPDATA/the-chief/tab-bridge on Windows) and tells agents to drive your real Chrome through it, including sites where you are signed in. Or a folder path to your own copy (tb.js + start-bridge). First time: chrome://extensions, Developer mode, Load unpacked, the ext folder inside it.

api_credit_fallback.title: API credit for Claude workers
api_credit_fallback.description: off (default): Claude workers always use your Claude login. on: a tier-routed worker that lands on Claude runs on the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in your user environment (paid API credit) while the day stays under api_daily_usd; then on your login.

api_daily_usd.title: API credit per day ($)
api_daily_usd.description: A day's spend on the API key, counted in ~/.claude/the-chief/hq/api-spend/<day>.jsonl by these workers. Used only when api_credit_fallback is on.
